title: Torsion objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a preadditive category that is linear over a commutative ring $R$,
and let $M\subseteq R$ be a submonoid. An object $X$ of $\mathcal T$ is *$M$-torsion* if
$m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X=0$ for some $m\in M$. The $M$-torsion objects form a property of
objects closed under isomorphisms.

proof.text:
If $e\colon X\cong Y$, then $m\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y=e^{-1}\circ(m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X)\circ e$, so
$m\cdot\mathrm{id}_X=0$ implies $m\cdot\mathrm{id}_Y=0$.

lean.note: The upstream definition is exactly the M-torsion object property: for a preadditive category C linear over a commutative ring R and M : Submonoid R, torsion M C X is ∃ m ∈ M, m • 𝟙 X = 0. The upstream instance instIsClosedUnderIsomorphismsTorsion supplies closure under isomorphisms, as required by the node.
